findings: EXECUTION-TIME SCOPE STALENESS: the runtime satisfies AUTH-INV-06 for status/revocation/expiry but NOT for scope. OrchestratorFlow._execute re-reads the registry (flow.py:971) and tests only is_active / id-in-revocations / is_expired on the fresh record (flow.py:975-985); it then builds ExecutionRequest with the PLANNING-TIME delegation snapshot (flow.py:999, passed in at flow.py:625 as the child issued during the planning authority gate), and ExecutionEngine.recheck_authority runs the authority gate against req.delegation (engine.py:302). Because control.authority.recheck_authority derives operations/resources/environments/prohibited_actions/requires_approval solely from the object it is handed (control/authority.py:197-209), a Human registry update that narrows or alters scope while leaving the delegation ACTIVE (e.g. scope_resources agents/** -> agents/cto/**, dropping code_write from operations, adding requires_approval: [destructive], lowering maximum_cost) is invisible at execution: the action proceeds under superseded scope. Delegation.version and Delegation.updated_at exist (orchestrator/foundation/contracts.py:224,226) but are never compared anywhere in control/authority.py, control/delegation.py, engine.py or flow.py, so there is no freshness binding on the authority record.

assumptions: FileDelegationProvider (state/registry/delegations.json via the O3 registry read) is the production authority seam, and a Human/authorized writer can change scope fields on an ACTIVE delegation without flipping status or expiry.
Registry writes are expected to bump version/updated_at (single-writer control plane, ADR 0002); not exercised here because the task is read-only.
docs/authority.md §4 intends scope to be re-evaluated against the current record at execution; if the intent is snapshot-scope-only, the doc and the code disagree rather than the code being wrong.
risks: STALE_AUTHORIZATION / TOCTOU_REVALIDATION_OMISSION on the scope dimension: AUTH-INV-02/04 containment is enforced only at issuance, so a post-planning narrowing of the grant does not re-gate an in-flight action.
Revocation semantics are partially misleading: revocation-by-id works, but 'quiet narrowing' (the more likely Human response to a misbehaving run) is equivalent to no revocation at execution time.
Test assurance gap: INT-02/INT-07/THREAT-009 prove expiry+revocation re-checks, which can be read as full execution-time authority freshness; the scope path is untested and therefore unproven.

Recovery path already passes the fresh record (flow.py:1296 self._execute(delegation_now, ...)), so normal and recovery executions use different authority bindings — an inconsistency that will make future gate changes drift.
structured.recommendation: Bind the execution-time re-check to the CURRENT registry record instead of the planning snapshot. Minimal change in OrchestratorFlow._execute: after provider.current(), fail closed unless delegation_now.id == delegation.id and (delegation_now.version, delegation_now.updated_at) == (delegation.version, delegation.updated_at) — on mismatch, STOP -> PRESERVE -> RE-GATE per AUTH-INV-06/DRIFT_AUTHORIZATION; or construct ExecutionRequest with delegation_now and re-derive the child scope from it. Add a regression test that leaves status ACTIVE but narrows scope_resources / adds requires_approval between planning and execution and asserts DENY, plus a static check that no execution path passes a planning-time delegation into ExecutionRequest.
